flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your c6-knight puts it where the white queen can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been moving your g8-knight to f6 because you can likely pin the knight to the king.
flags.critique: I traded knights. Queen takes back, material is even. Telling me I 'lose a knight' is a lie; the real Scotch lesson is I handed White a monster queen on d4. And Nf6 does not pin that knight to the king. It develops and hits e4. If you invent a pin, I stop trusting the rest.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your queen is the strongest move because the knight was undefended and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: I recaptured. That is not winning an undefended knight; it is finishing the trade you just scolded me for. The d-file pin is the d7-pawn to the queen, not 'to the rook.' Also the sentence is broken English: 'was undefended and then pin' sounds like two templates glued together.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b6 is a mistake, but moving your queen to f6 would be better because you skewer the white queen, exposing the white pawn.
flags.critique: Qf6 attacks the queen. That is the whole Scotch idea I needed. Calling it a skewer that 'exposes the white pawn' is coach-trying-too-hard. I am not playing this move to nibble b2. Teach me to challenge the centralized queen, not a tactic name that makes 1200s roll their eyes.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b4 is a blunder, but moving your knight to c3 would be better.
flags.critique: Plus-180 to minus-29 and you give me a shrug. Why is b4 a blunder? It is a random pawn lunge that does not develop, and Black can rip it with a5 or c5. 'Nc3 would be better' with zero because-clause is not coaching. It is a move name.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to d2 leaves your king with less protection. A better move would have been taking the pawn on g7 with your queen because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: You found Qxg7. Then you explained the move I played as king safety, which is not why this is a 500-centipawn blunder. Qd2 is a retreat that misses a hanging g7-pawn and the rook behind it. Lecture me about the free kingside, not 'less protection.'

flags.quote: Moving your c5-bishop to d4 leaves your pawn hanging to the white pawn. A better move would have been moving your c8-bishop to b7.
flags.critique: Which pawn? Which white pawn? You have now used this sentence twice. The threat is exf5. Bb7 does not save f5 either, so your 'better move' fails the problem you just named. Pick one lesson and make the suggestion match it.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d2 with your queen is the strongest move because you fork the white d3-bishop and the white c1-bishop and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: I took a queen with check. That is the lesson. You buried it under a bishop fork and 'defender of the white pawn' (which pawn?). When the capture is a queen, lead with the queen. The fork is a geometric afterthought I do not care about.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d2 with your c1-bishop leaves your a1-rook hanging to the black d4-bishop. A better move would have been taking the queen on d2 with your king.
flags.critique: The a1-rook hangs to Bd4 after Kxd2 too. The diagonal d4-c3-b2-a1 is still open. So you did not explain why the king recapture is better; you pretended it saves the rook. Teach the real difference: keep the bishop pair, king recapture, whatever it is, but do not invent a save that is not there.

flags.quote: Moving your king to d8 leaves your pawn hanging to the white pawn. A better move would have been taking the rook on a1 with your d4-bishop because the rook was undefended.
flags.critique: You named the free rook in the second sentence, then spent the first sentence on yet another unnamed pawn. I missed Bxa1. That is a 200-plus blunder. Stop changing the subject to a pawn when a rook is sitting on a1 undefended.

flags.quote: Moving your a1-rook to d1 is the strongest move because it saves your d1-rook from capture.
flags.critique: I moved the rook off a1. You told me that saves the d1-rook, which is the square I just arrived on. Say you got the rook off the bishop's diagonal before Bxa1. Destination-square naming turns a real save into a joke.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e4 with your f-pawn is the strongest move because you take the defender of the white d3-bishop.
flags.critique: e4 does not defend Bd3. White pawns capture diagonally forward; e4 covers d5 and f5. The bishop defends the pawn, not the other way around. You inverted the defender and taught me fake geometry.

flags.quote: Moving your a8-rook to b8 is a blunder, but moving your a8-rook to a7 would be better.
flags.critique: Five hundred centipawns, empty because-clause. The knight on d5 is eyeing b6 and c7; the bishop on e4 is loaded on the a8 diagonal. Tell me the fork or the hanging pawn. 'Ra7 would be better' is a spoiler without a lesson.

flags.quote: You are still winning, but moving your pawn to c4 creates a backward pawn to defend. A better move would have been moving your d2-bishop to f4 because you pin the pawn to the rook and it unveils an attack from your rook on the black d4-bishop.
flags.critique: I dropped 500 centipawns missing Bf4, which discovers the rook onto the d4-bishop and wins a piece. You opened with a backward-pawn lecture. Structure is not why this is a blunder. Lead with the hanging bishop. The pin-the-pawn clause is extra noise.

flags.quote: You are still winning, but taking the knight on f6 with your knight puts it where the black d4-bishop and pawn can take and you lose a knight.
flags.critique: Same lie as move 4: this is a recapture trade, not me hanging a knight. Black takes back, we swapped knights. If Bg5 was better, say you missed a pin and a discovered hit on d4. Do not tell me I lost a piece I just traded.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on d7 with your f5-bishop is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead.
flags.critique: I took a rook, king takes back, I am up the exchange, not 'a bishop.' Plus-200 is rook-for-bishop, and your label mapped it to a bishop. I know what an exchange is. Getting the material wrong at the moment I finally win something is insulting.

flags.quote: Moving your g1-knight to f3 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: Nf3 attacks the e5-pawn. That is the first Open Game lesson. 'Pressure on the center' is the same card you play on e4, e5, and d4. I already know knights go toward the middle. Tell me I am threatening to take.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: This is the Scotch. The point is to blow open the center and recapture with the knight. Identical center-control copy as Nf3. If you cannot name the opening idea, at least say you challenge e5 and open lines for the queen.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your f3-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Recapturing the pawn Black just took is not 'winning material' or some clever loot of an undefended pawn. It is the move the opening is built on. Call it a recapture. The wins_material reason is how you later tell me I 'lose a knight' on even trades.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to c5 leaves your pawn hanging to the white queen. A better move would have been moving your queen to f6.
flags.critique: Name g7. The queen on d4 is staring at g7 and the rook. 'Your pawn' could be any of five pawns. Qf6 is the right better-move (hits the queen and covers g7), but without the square I have to guess what I hung.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 is playable, but moving your knight to c3 would be better.
flags.critique: f3 weakens the king, takes the knight's best square, and does not develop. You listed saves_piece as a reason, which I cannot even map onto this move. Empty 'Nc3 would be better' again. Tell me why f3 is the cheap pawn-push it is.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f5 puts it at risk of attack from the white pawn. A better move would have been moving your c8-bishop to b7.
flags.critique: It is not 'at risk of attack.' e4 can take it. Say hanging. And Bb7 does not stop exf5, so once again the suggested move ignores the hanging pawn you mentioned. Also pawn_shield is the wrong concept when the pawn can just be captured.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to d3 is a blunder, but moving your queen to d5 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: 'Likely take a pawn' is weasel copy. Qd5 hits the hanging f5-pawn. Name f5. A 350-centipawn blunder is missing a capture, not a vibe that a pawn might fall. I hate 'likely' when the take is legal right now.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to b4 leaves your pawn hanging to the white pawn. A better move would have been moving your c8-bishop to b7.
flags.critique: Third copy of 'pawn hanging to the white pawn' plus the same Bb7 suggestion. Lichess called this a blunder; you called it a mistake. I still do not know which pawn. If f5 is still hanging, say f5, and stop recycling the line.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your pawn to d5 leaves your king with less pawn cover. A better move would have been moving your pawn to d6.
flags.critique: d5 hangs to c4. That is why d6 is better: it keeps the pawn. 'Less pawn cover' is a king-safety template on a hanging central pawn. I need 'c4 takes on d5,' not a shield lecture.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your king to c8 leaves your pawn hanging to the white d1-rook and pawn. A better move would have been moving your pawn to g5.
flags.critique: You named the attackers and still not the pawn. It is d5, already hanging on the file. g5 as the improvement needs a because: it kicks Bf4. Without that, I think you are randomly shoving kingside pawns while my d-pawn dies.

suggestions.title: Stop calling even trades a lost piece
suggestions.detail: Hanging and wins_material fire on the capturer the ply it recaptures, so Nxd4/Nxf6 become 'you lose a knight' and recaptures become 'the piece was undefended.' Net SEE with the captured unit before emitting hangingLossCopy or wins_material. A 1200 notices immediately that Qxd4 recaptures, they did not hang a knight.

suggestions.title: Put squares on hanging pawns
suggestions.detail: labeledPiece skips squares for pawns, so ignored_threat/hanging copy collapses to 'your pawn hanging to the white pawn' (plies 14, 20, 22, 26, 40, 42). Always include the square for pawns in problem copy. Learners cannot guess g7 vs f5 vs d5.

suggestions.title: Lead with the missed capture
suggestions.detail: When the suggested move wins material (Qxg7, Bxa1, Bf4 hitting Bd4, cxd5), do not pick king_more_exposed, backward_pawn, or pawn_shield as the played problem. CONCEPT_PRIORITY and pickProblemReasons should prefer missed hanging/capture over structure. This game's 500cp swings were explained as king safety and backward pawns.

suggestions.title: Never ship a blunder with no because
suggestions.detail: missedImprovementSentence with only a suggested SAN (b4, f3, Rb8) teaches nothing. If suggestedEffects are empty, pull a reason from the suggested line's first capture, check, or hanging reply. Blunders over 200cp must name a tactic or hanging unit.

suggestions.title: Check that the captured unit actually defends
suggestions.detail: fxe4 claimed to take the defender of Bd3; e4 does not attack d3. Gate removed_defender on the defender attacking newlyHanging. Also drop removed_defender from benefit copy when the capture is already a queen or the newly hanging unit is an unnamed pawn.

suggestions.title: Name saved pieces by origin, not destination
suggestions.detail: Rd1 became 'saves your d1-rook from capture' because savedHanging/retreatedToSafety uses the to-square. Keep the from-square (a1-rook) or drop the square for unique pieces. Same bug will tautologize every retreat.

suggestions.title: Do not invent pins and pawn-skewers
suggestions.detail: verifyLikelyTactics let Nf6 'likely pin the knight to the king' (false) and Qf6 'skewer the queen, exposing the pawn' (geometric x-ray, wrong lesson). Require a real pin line, and do not teach skewers whose rear target is a pawn when the front piece is a queen. Attack-the-queen should be capture/attack copy, not skewer.

suggestions.title: Label +200 as the exchange
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 200–249 to 'a bishop', so Bxd7+ (rook for bishop, SEE ~200) said 'a bishop ahead.' hangingLossCopy already calls 180–220 'the exchange'. Reuse that band in materialLabel. 1200s know rook-for-bishop is the exchange, not a bishop.

whatWorked: Nc6 as saving e5 is the right Open Game lesson.
b5 'saves your pawn from capture' after a5 actually matches the board.
Nc3 blocking Bd4's path to a1 is a real interposition lesson.
Nd5 unveiling the queen onto Qb4 is a clean discovered-attack explanation.
Nf6 forking Nd5 and Be4 is true and useful.
Re8 pinning Be4 to the king, then O-O getting out of it, is a coherent two-move story.
Qxg7 as the suggested move on Qd2 is the correct punchline even though the problem clause is wrong.
Bf4's discovered rook hit on Bd4 (as the improvement to c4) is the right tactic when it finally appears.
